subject: question on data setup for multi-season site occupancy models

messages.author: 7cae77e58c6f814b
messages.subject: question on data setup for multi-season site occupancy models
parts:
I have count data on a crustacean species.  The data were collected sporadically over a 5 year period.  That is, data were collected over multiple occasions (daily site visits) within some of the 20 seasons (5 years x 4 seasons per year) but not at all within other seasons.   Two questions on setting up a site x replicate visit x season 3-dimensional data array (patterned off of Kery and Schaub Section 13.5.2):

1.  The maximum number of daily site visits within any season was 5.  For seasons with 1-4 visits, I am assuming that NAs are entered into the count columns of the data array when they were not sampled. (?)

2. For seasons with no samples, which are chronologically after seasons that were sampled, I am assuming these these seasons are ignored rather than populating these rows in an array with NAs.

As an example of what I am proposing,  here is some fake data (below).

Regarding Question 1, season 1 had 5 repeat visits, season 2 had 2 repeat visits and season 4 had 1 visit.  The rest of the data cells in seasons 2 and 4 are populated with NAs.   

Regarding Question 2, Season 3 was not sampled, so there are no rows of data.  I am uneasy about populating a season in the array with all NAs if it was sampled at all but it appears that this might be necessary to get an estimation of site-specific colonization probability over the study.

Thank you for any thoughts,
Paul Rudershausen
